Hi, Daniel. I'd like to reserve the large meeting room for a client visit on Thursday afternoon. Is it available at three?
Let me check the calendar. There's a training session in there until two, but after that it's free for the rest of the day.
Perfect. Please book it for me from three to four thirty.
Done. It's on the calendar now. Do you want the projector set up too?
Yes, please. I'll be showing slides. I'm going to email you the names of the four visitors right now, so you can print their badges.
Great. I'll have the room, the projector and the badges ready by three on Thursday.

Hello, this is Marcus in the design team. I finished an evening course last month, and I'd like to be reimbursed for the tuition. Which form do I need?
All the forms moved to the staff portal in September. Log in, open the Benefits tab, and the course reimbursement form is right at the top.
Ah, so that's why it's no longer in the shared folder. Is there a deadline?
Yes. Claims for last month need to be in by the thirty-first, along with your receipt and your manager's approval.
That's tight. My manager's on holiday until the second of next month.
That's fine. Upload the receipt today, and I'll add a note to your file making it an exception, so it's fine if the approval comes in a few days late.
Great, thanks. I'll do that right after lunch.

Good evening. We're checking in. There should be two rooms under Brightwell Consulting.

Welcome. Yes, two single rooms for three nights. One thing before I give you your keys. The elevator on this side of the building is out of order tonight, so I've moved you from the ninth floor down to the second.
That's fine. Does the shuttle to the convention center still leave at eight tomorrow?
It does, from the main entrance. Just show the driver your room key.
Great. Could we also have a late checkout on Friday? Our flight isn't until seven in the evening.
I can extend it to two o'clock at no extra charge. Just come to the front desk on Friday morning and remind us.
Perfect. Then I'll book a taxi to the airport for half past four.

Hana, since this morning's update, half the warehouse can't log in to the inventory system. The help desk has over thirty tickets.
I've seen them. It's the new security patch. It rejects any password with a symbol in it, like an exclamation mark. I can roll back to the old version in twenty minutes.
Please do. The afternoon shift starts at two, and they can't ship orders without it.
Understood. After that, I'll fix the patch and test it on the staging server before we release it again.
This morning's update went through staging as well.
Fair point. The test accounts on staging don't use symbols, so the bug never showed up. This time I'll test it with a few accounts that have symbols in the passwords.
Good. Message me when the rollback's done, and I'll tell the help desk.

That's all right. Show them to the back room, hand out the menus, and take them some water and bread baskets while Priya sets the long table.

Nadia, your two o'clock patient, Mr. Beltran, just called. He's stuck in traffic, so he'll be about twenty minutes late.
That's a problem. My two-thirty is a new patient assessment, and those take the full hour, so I can't push it back.
Shall I offer him another day? There's a free slot on Thursday morning.
Yes, try that first. And if Thursday doesn't suit him, I can see him at four this afternoon. My last patient of the day just cancelled.
Right, I'll call him back now. One more thing. The supplier says the new treatment table won't arrive until Friday.
Honestly, I'm not surprised. Every delivery they've sent us this year has been late. We'll keep using the old table until then.

Hi, I'm looking for a two-bedroom apartment. My lease at my current place ends on November fifteenth, so I need somewhere I can move into before then.
We have a couple of two-bedroom units coming up, but only one of them is ready before the fifteenth. The other won't be free until December.
Then I'd like to see the one that's ready first. Is the rent negotiable at all?
The owner sets the rent, and he won't go any lower. He does include parking and water, though, which saves most tenants about a hundred dollars a month.
That helps. Could I take a look at it today?
Not today, I'm afraid. The current tenant has asked for a day's notice, so I'll call her right now and then text you a time for tomorrow.

Oscar, I'm closing the books for the third quarter, and your team's travel spending is eighteen percent over forecast. Can you explain the gap?
Most of it is the regional trade show. It took place in June, but the hotel and the venue only invoiced us in July, so the whole cost landed in this quarter.

I see. But a cost belongs in the quarter the event happened, not the quarter the bill arrives. Could you send me the booking confirmations? They'll prove the actual dates, and I'll move the cost back.
Of course. I'll pull them together this afternoon. Will that bring the variance down?
It should fall below ten percent, so you won't have to explain it to the board next month.
Well, that's one meeting I'm glad to skip. You'll have the confirmations by three.

Yes. The motor on the sealing unit is overheating, so it won't restart. I've ordered a new motor, and the supplier says it'll be delivered on Thursday morning.
Thursday? That's a problem. The Kessler order has to go out on Friday. Could we pack those boxes on line two until then?
We could. Line two is set up for the small boxes right now, but I can change the settings. It'll take me about an hour.
Please do that now. While you're working on it, I'll walk over to the warehouse and let the team know the Kessler boxes will be coming from line two instead.
No problem. I'll call you as soon as it's ready.

I know. I reminded them why we picked the original date, but their head office has already decided.

Leo, I've just compared the Northgate Office Supplies invoice with the delivery note. The invoice lists forty chairs, but the warehouse only signed for thirty-two.
So they've billed us for eight chairs that never arrived. Can you email their accounts team today and ask for a corrected invoice?
I will. The trouble is, the payment's due on Monday, and our contact there is away until the end of the month.
Then we won't pay yet. Hold the payment until the figures match. I'll explain the delay to the finance director myself.
Should I mention that in the email to Northgate as well?
Yes, say we're holding payment until the invoice is corrected. That tends to get a quick response, even when someone's away.

Attention, Harlow Home shoppers. Thanks for shopping with us today. From cookware to curtains, you'll find it all here. Until three o'clock this afternoon, every item in our bedding department on the second floor is twenty percent off. That means sheets, pillows, blankets and duvet covers. The discount is applied automatically at the register, so there's nothing extra to do. One quick reminder. Our gift-wrapping counter near the main entrance closes at six this evening, two hours before the store itself closes at eight. If you'd like a purchase wrapped, please stop by the counter before six. And if you want to hear about future sales before anyone else, ask any cashier how to sign up for our free text alerts. It takes less than a minute. Thanks again for shopping at Harlow Home, and enjoy your afternoon.

Hi, this is Daniel calling from Brightwater Dental, and this message is for Ms. Okafor. I'm sorry, but we need to move your appointment with Dr. Lindqvist. It was booked for Thursday at half past two, but the doctor will be away at a training course that afternoon. We have two other times open: Friday at nine in the morning, or Tuesday at four in the afternoon. Please call us back and tell us which one you'd prefer, and we'll confirm it straight away. If neither time works for you, please call us anyway, and we'll find another day together. Also, when you come in, please bring your new insurance card so we can update your file. Sorry again for the change, and we'll speak soon.

Is your laptop taking forever to start up? Does your phone battery barely last till lunchtime? Bring it to Northgate Device Repair. Our certified technicians fix cracked screens, worn-out batteries and slow laptops, and most jobs are finished the same day. Every repair comes with a six-month guarantee. And here's our special offer for March. Book any screen repair on our website, and we'll replace your battery at half price. That's a saving of up to sixty dollars, but only until the thirty-first, so don't wait. You'll find our shop on Carrow Street in Elmbrook, open seven days a week. Can't get to us? No problem. For a flat fee of twelve dollars, our courier will pick up your device from your home or office and bring it back when it's fixed. Visit our website to book today. Northgate Device Repair. Fixed fast, fixed right.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Marwood Bicycle Works. I'm Ethan, and I'll be your guide for this morning's visitor tour. Before we go through those doors, a few things. You've each got a printed schedule, and we'll follow it, with one change. One area is closed for maintenance today, so the eleven twenty stop is cancelled. That means you'll have extra time in the quality lab to watch frames being tested. On the floor, safety glasses stay on at all times, and please stay inside the yellow lines. Photos are fine, except near the welding stations, where a flash can distract the operators. Finally, some visitors save their questions for the end. You don't need to. If something catches your eye, stop me right there. I'd rather you ask than wonder. All right, let's head in.

Thanks, everyone. Next on the agenda is the Lumen water bottle, and I want to propose some changes to the spring campaign before we run it again in summer. Our social media posts reached three hundred thousand people, roughly double what we projected. But only two percent of those people clicked through to the product page, and our target was five. So people enjoyed the posts; they just weren't moved to buy. I read through the comments, and the question that came up again and again was the price, which we never showed. So for summer, every post will state the price up front, and we'll add a short video of the bottle keeping ice frozen for twenty-four hours. Mei, could you draft three versions of the video script by Friday? We'll choose one on Monday. Then on Tuesday, I'll take our budget request to the finance team.

Good morning, and thanks for staying with us on Harbor Radio. If you're making weekend plans, here's some good news. The Pinecrest Farmers' Market is back this Saturday after its winter break. More than forty stalls will line Mill Street, selling fresh produce, baked goods, and handmade crafts. The market opens at eight in the morning and closes at one in the afternoon. Please note that there'll be no parking on Mill Street itself that day. Organizers are asking visitors to use the free lot behind the public library, which is just a two-minute walk from the market. A local band will play live from ten o'clock. And if you can, bring your own bags, because stall holders have only a limited supply of paper ones. Now, stay tuned. Dana is up next with the morning traffic report.

Thank you for calling Brookfield Motor Services. I'm afraid you've reached us outside our opening hours. We're open Monday to Friday, from eight in the morning until six in the evening, and on Saturdays until one o'clock. If you'd like to book a service or a repair, or change a booking you've already made, please leave your name, your registration number and a daytime phone number after the tone, and someone from our front desk will call you back on the next working day. Morning, everyone, and welcome to the Oakbridge Hotel kitchen. Before your first shift, I'll run through a few safety basics. The flat-top grills stay hot long after they're switched off, so treat every metal surface as hot unless you've checked. Knives go back in the block the moment you've finished with them, never in the sink, where the next person can't see them. If you spill something, mop it up right away and put the yellow cone out. The first-aid kit is on the wall beside the walk-in fridge. If you cut or burn yourself, tell me or the sous chef, Luis, straight away, even if it seems minor. I'd rather hear about ten small cuts than find out about one big one later. If anything's unclear, ask me or Luis at any time. Now grab an apron and let's get started.

Thank you, everyone. Before dessert comes out, I have one more thing to do, and it's the best part of my evening. Twenty years ago this month, a young engineer joined Fenmoor Systems to look after a single server room. Today, she manages a team of thirty people in three countries. I'm talking about Priya Nandan. Priya, half the people in this room have phoned you at two in the morning when a system went down, and you've never once complained. Many of you may not know that she also started our graduate mentoring scheme, which more than half of our new graduates have now completed. Priya, please come up and accept this award for twenty years of service. And before anyone starts worrying, no, she is not retiring. She's staying right here with us, and she asked me to make that very clear. Please give her a warm welcome.
